html:
A Yemeni journalist, politician and human rights activist who shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2011. She was the first Arab woman to win a Nobel Prize.

In 2005 she co-founded Women Journalists Without Chains, a group that campaigns for press freedom in Yemen. She led weekly sit-ins in the capital Sanaa against President Ali Abdullah Saleh, who had ruled since 1978, and was arrested several times.

When the Arab Spring reached Yemen in 2011, she became the best known face of the uprising, and Yemenis called her the mother of the revolution. Saleh agreed to hand over power later that year. She shared the Nobel Peace Prize that year with two Liberian women, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and Leymah Gbowee, for their work for women's rights and peace. At 32 she was then the youngest Peace laureate.

Yemen's hopes soon gave way to civil war. She has lived mostly abroad since, and has kept speaking against both sides of the war.
sum: A Yemeni journalist, politician and human rights activist who shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2011. She was the first Arab woman to win a Nobel Prize.
